title: Ahhotep I
summary: Ahhotep was a 17th Dynasty Egyptian queen, wife of Seqenenre Tao II and mother of Ahmose, founder of the 18th Dynasty. A Karnak stele set up by Ahmose credits her in the war against the Hyksos. A gilded coffin with jewellery and weapons found at Dra Abu el-Naga at Thebes in 1859 is linked to her, but scholars debate whether one queen or two named Ahhotep are involved.

uncertainty.note: Team Queens gives "c. 1580-1530 BC"; Archaeology magazine places her in the 17th Dynasty, "ca. 1635-1550 b.c." (the dynasty, not her lifespan). Dates are approximate and tied to uncertain Egyptian chronology.

as_recorded.value: Mariette's team found the gilded coffin at Dra Abu el-Naga, Thebes, in 1859
A. Mariette found her funeral vault in 1859 at Dra Abu el-Naga in Thebes

where.modern_name: Dra Abu el-Naga necropolis, Luxor (ancient Thebes), Egypt (pinned to the site of the gilded-coffin burial attributed to her; the attribution to Ahhotep I versus a second Ahhotep is debated)
where.historical_name: Thebes, seat of the 17th Dynasty, Egypt, in the Second Intermediate Period

importance.justification: Two sources describe a Karnak stele erected by Ahmose that credits her with a role in the Hyksos war, and a major burial find in 1859.

reviewer_note: Whether the Dra Abu el-Naga coffin belongs to Ahhotep I (mother of Ahmose) or a second Ahhotep is debated in the Archaeology magazine article, so confidence is contested. Her relation to Kamose is not stated on the pages opened. Dates come from one popular source. Pinned at the burial site, not at Karnak.
